body:
Devon Ricci: Sarah, Jenny, Miguel — thanks for making time. Sarah, thanks for pulling Miguel into this one. Miguel, this is our first time on a call together.

Miguel Ramos: Nice to meet you both. I run our bilingual support operations. About thirty-two percent of our customer base speaks Spanish as a first language, and we've been running a separate Spanish call queue for years.

Sarah Kwon: The loyalty expansion Voxly launched in Q1 has been great — Jenny, you want to hit the numbers?

Jenny Alvarez: Sure. Loyalty containment is at forty-nine percent since launch. Tier-status inquiries are almost entirely automated now. But — thirty-eight percent of our loyalty members primarily speak Spanish and right now those calls all fall out of the bot into the Spanish human queue. We need Spanish language support in the bot.

Elena Sokolova: I've been waiting for this conversation. Let me tell you where we are on Spanish. Voice_agent_v2 with Spanish support is in beta right now with two customers. GA target is September first. It's Latin American Spanish primarily — Mexico, Central America accents — with a code-switching mode that handles English-Spanish mid-sentence.

Miguel Ramos: Code-switching is huge. That's actually the hardest part. Our customers frequently switch mid-sentence — 'my número de cuenta is one two three' — and legacy IVRs completely fall apart on that.

Elena Sokolova: The beta handles that well. I can share sample recordings under NDA if you want to hear.

Miguel Ramos: Please. That would help me sell this internally.

Sarah Kwon: Elena, is there any way we get on the beta before September?

Elena Sokolova: Honestly, we've capped the beta at two customers because we're iterating fast. But I'd consider a third if you're willing to accept beta-level SLA and give us weekly feedback. Meridian's volume would give us great signal.

Jenny Alvarez: I'd sign up for that. We can dedicate someone from my team to weekly feedback.

Miguel Ramos: I can put two of my supervisors on it. They know the failure modes cold.

Elena Sokolova: Perfect. Devon, let's spin up a beta agreement. Miguel, one specific question — how do you want the bot to detect the caller's language? Automatic detection from the first utterance, or opt-in via IVR menu?

Miguel Ramos: Automatic. Any explicit language selection step is a friction point that costs us CSAT. The current IVR asks 'para español, oprima dos' and we hate it.

Elena Sokolova: Auto-detect it is. We have a language identification model that fires on the first three seconds of speech, ninety-six percent accuracy on our test set.

Sarah Kwon: What about accented English speakers? Say a customer with a heavy accent — the bot won't switch them to Spanish, right?

Elena Sokolova: Correct. It detects language, not accent. English with a Spanish accent stays in English.

Miguel Ramos: Good. That matters.

Devon Ricci: Timeline question — if we start beta on Meridian in early July, what does GA look like on your side, Sarah?

Sarah Kwon: If beta goes well, full Spanish rollout in October, ahead of holiday peak.

Elena Sokolova: That aligns perfectly with our GA.

Sarah Kwon: Contract implication?

Devon Ricci: Beta usage is included in your current contract at no additional charge. Post-GA we'd add Spanish as a language module, which is priced at fifteen percent of your annual contract value or a fifty-thousand-dollar minimum, whichever is higher.

Sarah Kwon: We can work with that.

Devon Ricci: Great. Elena will send the beta agreement, Miguel identifies his two supervisors, and Jenny picks a Loyalty person for the feedback loop. Sound good?

Sarah Kwon: Perfect. Thanks Elena — this is exactly what we needed to hear.

Jenny Alvarez: Elena, one product question — will the Spanish bot handle our loyalty program terminology? Words like puntos, canjear, nivel gold — those are all specialized to us.

Elena Sokolova: We'll do a terminology tuning pass during beta. Send us your glossary and we'll build a specialized lexicon for Meridian.

Jenny Alvarez: Perfect.

Miguel Ramos: What about regional dialect variation? Our Mexican customers and our Puerto Rican customers speak differently.

Elena Sokolova: The base model handles both well in testing. We haven't seen accent-related failure modes but we'll be monitoring closely during beta.

Miguel Ramos: Good.

Sarah Kwon: What's the exit criteria for beta to GA on our side? Meaning what metrics do we need to hit to feel comfortable going full production.

Elena Sokolova: I'd suggest containment rate within five points of your English bot, and CSAT parity with your Spanish human agents. If both hit, you're ready.

Sarah Kwon: Reasonable.

Miguel Ramos: One risk I want to flag — our Spanish human queue currently has ninety-second average wait times. If the bot gets popular fast, our fallback path might get overwhelmed.

Elena Sokolova: Fair concern. We can dial the bot's coverage up gradually — start at ten percent of Spanish calls, scale as you gain confidence.

Miguel Ramos: That's what I'd want.

Devon Ricci: We'll set up a Spanish-specific dashboard so you can watch the metrics in real time.

Sarah Kwon: Perfect.

Elena Sokolova: Thank you all. Excited to have Meridian in the beta.

Sarah Kwon: Thanks Elena. Talk soon.
